`EigenmodeSim` finds the lowest resonant modes of a layout with Palace and,
when you ask, how much of each mode's energy sits in each surface film, each
bulk region and each port: its energy participation (EPR). This page is the
reference of its calls and of the Surface-EPR margins. The
[Palace modes guide](../../guides/modes-palace.qmd) runs a study, and the
[Xmon example](../../guides/xmon/palace.qmd) adds EPR. The mesh settings and
the convergence declaration are shared with Electrostatic and are on
[Palace Electrostatic, mesh and convergence](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd).

## The calls {#eigenmode-calls}

From the [Palace modes guide](../../guides/modes-palace.qmd):

```python
sim = EigenmodeSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/public-xmon-palace-modes"))
sim.set_eigenmode(num_modes=2, target=2e9, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)
sim.set_mesh(recipe=FeatureRecipe(), quality_threshold=0.01)
sim.set_numerical(amr_max_passes=0)
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
```

| Call | What it sets |
|---|---|
| `set_plan(snapshot)` | The prepared `GeometryPlan`, with its vacuum, Surface-EPR films and lumped elements. |
| `set_output_dir(path)` | The run folder. |
| `set_eigenmode(*, num_modes=10, target=None, tolerance=1e-6, save=0)` | How many modes, the frequency to search from (`target`, in hertz), the eigensolver tolerance and how many modes' fields to save. |
| `set_epr_request(*, surface_interfaces=None, bulk_domain_ids=None, port_names=None)` | Which participations are reported; see [Selections](#selection-and-physical-meaning). |
| `set_route`, `set_mesh`, `set_numerical`, `set_convergence` | As for Electrostatic: [the calls](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#electrostatic-calls), [mesh settings](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls), [convergence](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration). |
| `input_summary()`, `mesh()`, `write_config()`, `prepare_handoff(...)` | As for Electrostatic. |

Read the settings back with `sim.numerical` (a `NumericalControls`),
`sim.surface_epr_specs` (the plan's films, or `None`) and `sim.epr_request`
(or `None` before `set_epr_request`). Units: target frequency in hertz,
lengths in micrometres, inductance in henries. A model needs a vacuum region;
ordinary Eigenmode needs no Surface EPR, lumped elements or EPR request.

## AMR defaults {#eigenmode-mesh-and-amr-defaults}

A new `EigenmodeSim` writes `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal=true`. Before
`write_config()`, give `amr_max_passes` with `set_numerical(...)`:

| `amr_max_passes` | Also needed |
|---|---|
| `0` | Nothing: no adaptive refinement. |
| A positive number, no convergence declaration | `amr_tolerance` and `amr_update_fraction` |
| A positive number, with a convergence declaration | `amr_update_fraction`; a stated `amr_tolerance` is refused |

In a later `set_numerical(...)` call, an omitted argument behaves as follows:

| Arguments | When omitted |
|---|---|
| `ksp_type`, `amr_max_passes`, `amr_nonconformal`, `amr_nc_levels`, `amr_tolerance`, `amr_update_fraction` | keep their current values |
| `order`, `tolerance`, `max_iterations`, `solver_type`, `preconditioner`, `device`, `save_adapt_iterations`, `save_adapt_mesh`, `estimator_mg`, `output_paraview`, `output_grid_function` | return to their defaults |

`EigenmodeSim(numerical=NumericalControls(order=2))` holds the same settings
as `EigenmodeSim()` followed by `set_numerical(order=2)`. These are input
settings, not recommendations.

## Convergence on Eigenmode {#eigenmode-convergence}

`EigenmodeSim.set_convergence` takes `ModeFrequency`, `SurfaceEpr` and
`ErrorIndicator`, defined in the
[convergence declaration](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration):

```python
from scgsim.palace import ErrorIndicator, ModeFrequency, SurfaceEpr

sim.set_numerical(amr_max_passes=8, amr_update_fraction=0.7)
sim.set_convergence(
    ModeFrequency(modes=[1]).within(percent=0.001),
    SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA", margin_um=1.0).within(percent=2),
    ErrorIndicator().below(1e-2),
)
```

A mode is a number from 1 to `num_modes`. A Surface-EPR type must have a spec
on the plan and must not be left out by `set_epr_request(surface_interfaces=...)`.
An `amr_tolerance` stated once stays until the simulation is built again, and
`write_config()` refuses it together with a declaration. The
[stop at convergence](palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-stop) is the
same as for Electrostatic.

## Lumped ports {#lumped-ports}

Each lumped element of the plan
([`set_lumped_elements`](geometry-plan.qmd#lumped-elements)) becomes one
Palace lumped port, numbered as the plan numbers it: `P1` is the first. A
`LumpedElement` carries its R, L and C as Palace's `R`, `L` and `C`, a
parallel circuit; a `LumpedPort` carries its impedance as `R`, a load, so the
mode's Q is the loaded Q. No port is excited. An authored sheet the plan
declares nothing on is not in the model. Palace needs each port to be a
rectangle, so `mesh()`
gives Palace the central rectangle of the drawn sheet and joins the two end
pieces to the conductors they land on.
[Lumped ports are made rectangles](../supported-geometry.qmd#lumped-port-rectangle)
shows how the cuts are chosen, with the Xmon's junction port as a worked
example. The sheet must land on exactly two conductors of two Nets; otherwise
`plan.prepare()` raises `ValueError` naming the element, its sheet's layer and
its place. A conductor without a Net counts as a Net of its own.

## What an EPR request selects {#selection-and-physical-meaning}

`set_epr_request` chooses what is reported:

| Argument | Selects | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `surface_interfaces` | Surface films | `"MA"` (metal-air), `"MS"` (metal-substrate), `"SA"` (substrate-air) |
| `bulk_domain_ids` | Bulk regions | The SGB volume names of `Domains.Postprocessing.Energy` |
| `port_names` | Ports | The names of the plan's lumped elements, their sheets' names |

`None` selects everything, `()` selects nothing, and an unknown name is
refused when the configuration is written or the result is read. For example,
`set_epr_request(surface_interfaces=["MA"], port_names=())` reports the
metal-air participation and no port. Selecting less does not remove a region
or a port from the model, and does not change the normalization.

### Surface films {#surface-film-inputs-and-native-material-side}

Each Surface-EPR spec on the plan gives its film: exactly one of `thickness`
(model units) or `film_thickness_m` (metres), exactly one of `permittivity` or
a dielectric `material_id`, and optionally `loss_tangent`; an unknown loss
tangent stays unknown, not zero. Palace evaluates each type on its own side of
the surface:

| Type | Field it uses | Side |
|---|---|---|
| `MA` | Normal electric field | Vacuum side |
| `MS` | Normal field, weighted by the substrate permittivity | Substrate side |
| `SA` | Tangential and normal field, with the film permittivity | Vacuum side |

Choose the type that matches the interface you model. How SCGSim writes these
rows for Palace is in [the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#surface-film-producer).

## Surface-EPR margins {#surface-epr-margins}

An inset margin $m$ selects the part of a surface at least $m$ µm from the
nearest *gap edge*: an edge of a conductor that faces exposed substrate.
Distance is measured only from gap edges, in the plane of the surface; an edge
on the model boundary, an edge where two conductors touch and an edge with
only vacuum beside it do not count. SGB cuts each margin into the model as a
band boundary, so a stock Palace 0.18.1 integrates the rows; no special Palace
build is needed. [Surface EPR](../../concepts/surface-epr.qmd) explains why the
part near the gap edges is set apart.

::: {.callout-important title="Set Surface EPR on the plan"}
Margins are geometry. Give the specs to `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` before
`plan.prepare()`; the simulation reads them from the snapshot `set_plan`
binds. A plan prepared with other specs discards the mesh, configuration and
handoff, and `mesh()` must run again. A plan without specs gets no bands and
no Surface-EPR rows.
:::

For example, a spec `"MA"` with `inset_margins_um=(0.5, 1.0)` on the square
pad of the [First simulation](../../start/first-simulation.qmd) (a 200 µm pad
in a 20 µm gap) gives three `MA` rows: the whole metal-air surface; the part
0.5 µm or more from a gap edge; and the part 1.0 µm or more from it. To
integrate them, SGB cuts the surface into the strips 0 to 0.5 µm and 0.5 to
1.0 µm from each gap edge, the bands, and the rest beyond 1.0 µm.

**The rows are alternatives.** Each margin row covers the bands from its
margin outward, so it overlaps the whole-surface row and the other margin
rows. Read each row on its own and never add them. A face without a gap edge,
such as the underside of a substrate, has no bands and is covered only by the
whole-surface row; the manifest lists the faces SGB skipped.

Each spec takes these margin keys next to its film:

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inset_margins_um` | Strictly increasing positive margins in µm, on every face of the spec's type. Every band must be at least 10 grid steps wide (10 nm on a 1 nm grid): the first band is the first margin, each next band the difference of two margins. A narrower band is refused with `ValueError` before the build. Leave it out for the whole-surface row only. |
| `inset_margins_by_entity_um` | `{entity_id: [margins]}` for `MA` and `MS`: each named conductor takes its own margins, and the rest of the type keeps `inset_margins_um`. It costs one extra geometry build to find the conductors' faces. A named conductor with no face of that type raises `ValueError` from `mesh()`. Not for `SA`, which has no owning conductor. |
| `face_kinds` | Limits the spec to some of `"sheet"`, `"top"`, `"bottom"` and `"interface"`. Side walls are never banded, so `"sidewall"` is refused when the spec asks for margins. |
:::

A margin of `0` is refused: the whole-surface row already covers it. Every
margin must be a whole number of grid steps.

**One face, one set of margins.** A Route A sheet carries both an `MA` and an
`MS` row, so when both specs reach it they must give it the same margins.
Different margins on one sheet are refused, naming the conductor, the face and
both sets.

Each row has a group name of the form `<type>::<entity>__<face kind>[::band=k]`,
for example `MA::pad__top::band=1`, with the face kind `top`, `bottom`,
`sidewall`, `sheet` or `interface`. On a Route A sheet the rows are
`MA::pad__sheet::band=k` where vacuum touches it and `MS::pad__sheet::band=k`
where a dielectric does. Read band membership from the index map rather than
from the names; the map's fields are in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#index-map-rows).

## What a result holds {#results-and-offline-analysis}

`resolve_palace_result(run_dir, expected_handoff_id=...)` reads a completed
run; `result.epr_result()` gives its EPR as a `PalaceEprResult`, which you can
save with `to_payload()` and read back with `resolve_epr_result(path)`.
`reanalyze_epr(result, surface_defaults=..., group_overrides=...)` changes the
loss assumptions without solving again, and `show_epr(result, mode=...)` draws
it; neither starts Palace. [Change loss assumptions without solving](../../guides/offline-loss.qmd)
shows both.

A result holds exactly the `num_modes` modes you asked for. Palace may report
more converged modes; SCGSim keeps modes 1 to `num_modes` in Palace's order. A
table with fewer rows, or whose modes are not numbered 1, 2, … in order, is
refused.

### An infinite Q {#native-eigenmode-q}

When Palace reports a mode's Q as infinite (`+inf` in `eig.csv`, a mode with no
loss in the model), the result keeps it and the report labels it
**native-reported infinite Q**, with no finite Q for that mode. The mode's
frequency and energies are read as usual. This is the only value of
infinity SCGSim accepts in a Palace table.

Palace's port participation is signed and depends on the phase convention; it
is not AEDT's pair of non-negative inductive and capacitive participations.
[Surface EPR](../../concepts/surface-epr.qmd) explains normalization and loss,
and [Reading a run](report-model.qmd) what the report shows.
